title: Marlowe & Finch Home Delivery Terms: What Makes One Booking
content:
**Clause.** A customer of Marlowe & Finch Home Delivery may have any number of delivery bookings; there is no maximum number of bookings per customer. The large items of one order going to one address travel on one booking, and the fee is charged on that booking. Items of separate orders, or one order split to two addresses at the customer's request, are separate bookings, each paying its own fee.

## The clause as conditions and results

| Items to be delivered | Bookings | Fees |
|---|---|---|
| Large items of one order, all to one address | One booking | One fee, on that booking |
| Large items of two separate orders | A separate booking for each order | Each booking pays its own fee |
| One order split to two addresses at the customer's request | A separate booking for each address | Each booking pays its own fee |

## Points of judgement

- **Is there a limit on how many deliveries a customer may have booked?** No. The number of bookings per customer has no maximum.
- **What decides whether items share a booking?** The order and the address together. The large items share a booking when they belong to one order and go to one address.
- **Does a split of one order to two addresses still share one fee?** No. Where the customer asks for one order to go to two addresses, each address is its own booking and each booking pays its own fee.

## Illustrations (hypothetical orders)

- One order with a sofa and two armchairs, all to one home: one booking, one fee.
- Two orders placed on different days, both to the same home: two bookings, each with its own fee.
- One order with a bed for the customer's home and a dresser that the customer asks to send to a second address: two bookings, each with its own fee.
